K1.rule: F1 holdout feasible strictly higher on at least 2 of 3 seeds and lower on none

K2.rule: pooled feasible over the seeds; improved requires neither pooled count to fall

judgement.rule: improved iff K1 and K2 (both pooled counts do not fall); K1 with a falling pooled count is mixed, never improved; the round23 rule "any seed larger = improved" is retired

replaces.note: round23 recorded -1/+1/0 and a lower total; under K1 that is not improved

K3.rule: mirror-group toward rate on the F1 holdout, canonical motion toward the gap

K4.rule: in-gap at wall_frame-1 and the signed parking error in canonical px

flip_rate.note: mirror_toward_rate is the fraction of mirror-group cells whose canonical motion points at the gap: that is the direction flip this round is about, because the same screen-right prior is wrong there and right in the base group

K5.rule: auxiliary head on the held-out geometry: per-seed accuracy, balanced accuracy and the 2x2 confusion; "learned" requires all three seeds above 0.5 balanced accuracy

learned_but_unused.rule: the round23 comparison this round must report: mirror cells where the auxiliary head read the required direction but the policy moved away
learned_but_unused.reading: if the head reads the required direction and the policy still moves away, the label definition was not the binding constraint: the coupling is; if the head stops reading it, the label itself is not learnable from the GRU state at this budget

holdout.executor: unchanged R18 policies()/causal_loop()/outcome() on the same worlds, executed here
holdout.rule: if ANY of the six R18 baselines is feasible on ANY validation event the R18 filter has failed on the holdout side: report it verbatim and withhold the learning conclusion

design.task: from the GRU state predict whether the safe gap lies left or right OF THE PLAYER, i.e. which sign of action closes the distance to the slot: label = sign(gap screen centre - player screen x), gap from round21.telegraph_gap(s) (privileged world parameter), player x from the frozen teacher trajectory (train) or the checkpoint's own trajectory (scoring); the label is read at the first row of the telegraph window
design.rule_text: the sign is taken at the FIRST decision row whose logical frame lies inside round21.telegraph_window(s) = [wall_frame-45, wall_frame) and applied to every supervised row of that event; per-row signs, flip rows and flip frames are recorded for every event and reported, and the per-row variant is not tried
design.supervision: the rows whose logical frame 2*i lies inside round21.telegraph_window(s) = [wall_frame-45, wall_frame)
design.rows: the preview-window decisions only, for every event
design.seen: the stored round21 training features of the six F1 train events: exactly the rows the auxiliary loss trained on, so this is fit
design.holdout: the six F1 validation events, each replayed along that checkpoint's own stored closed-loop trajectory, re-rendered from its own x trace; the label is the sign at that trajectory's first preview row and is never an input
design.chance: 0.5 on the frozen teacher table (3 left / 3 right on both splits); a checkpoint whose own trajectory flips the sign would move its cell label, and that is reported per cell rather than hidden
design.label_use: the label exists only inside the training loss and inside this scoring function; `PrivNetwork` (the closed loop) is the unmodified parent class and cannot read it

reference.note: round23 measured the same probe on ITS label (gap centre above 192) and got sweep means 0.826 (A) / 0.619 (X); the target of this round is a different binary variable, so only the arm-to-arm comparison and the whole lambda sweep are read

design.target: binary: is the gap screen centre right of the player, at the first preview row
design.rows: the preview-window decisions of the six F1 validation events, from the replay
design.fit: ridge on standardised inputs with an intercept, leave one geometry group out
design.caveat: 132 rows against 256 dimensions and a label that is constant within an event: the probe separates events as much as frames, so only the whole lambda sweep and the arm-to-arm comparison are read, never a single value

usage.note: one row per (network, F1 validation event); `aux_*` is the auxiliary head on the replayed pixels, `policy_*` is the stored closed loop of the same checkpoint; a high aux correctness with a low policy toward count is the "the task was learned, the behaviour did not use it" reading, cell by cell

agreement.note: the label never predicts hold, so a hold first action is counted separately and excluded from the rate; F2/F3 worlds have no gap and therefore no label

labels.note: the holdout label is a function of the checkpoint's own visible x, so it is recomputed per checkpoint; this table is the measurement of how far that label drifted from the frozen teacher trajectory it was defined on

prediction.note: the masked argmax actually taken, from the stored rows; per event over all 80 decisions and over the telegraph-window decisions only

base_bias.note: the frozen baseline (B0) is the policy head the residual offset is built on; its screen preference on the identical renders is the prior this round is testing against

rule.note: the teacher trajectory is used here; a checkpoint's own trajectory is scored with the same rule and its flips are reported in probes.json

agreement.note: the label never predicts hold, so a hold first action is counted separately and excluded from the rate; F2/F3 worlds have no gap and therefore no label

round23_collinearity.note: `round23_side` is round23's label (gap centre above 192); `player_screen_half` is the player's own visible x above 192 at the same row. Where the two coincide, round23's target was a statement about the player, not about the gap

round23_reference.label: round23 label = gap screen centre above x=192 (the playfield centre), not above the player

comparison.note: round23's rule was "any seed larger = improved"; this round replaces it with K1 and the mixed verdict

round23_reference.behaviour: round23: screen directions 12R/3L/3hold (A) -> 17R/1L/0hold (X); mirror toward rate 3/9 -> 1/9; the auxiliary head read the mirror side correctly in 8/9 cells while the policy moved away in 8/9

K1.rule: F1 holdout feasible strictly higher on at least 2 of 3 seeds and lower on none

K2.rule: pooled feasible over the seeds; improved requires neither pooled count to fall

comparison.rule: improved iff K1 and K2 (both pooled counts do not fall); K1 with a falling pooled count is mixed, never improved; the round23 rule "any seed larger = improved" is retired

replaces.note: round23 recorded -1/+1/0 and a lower total; under K1 that is not improved

comparison.note: three seed pairs, six F1 validation events each; X minus A; descriptive only. K1/K2 above are the frozen rule; the round23 rule that called -1/+1/0 improved is retired

limitations: n=3 seeds and 7 validation groups; the 14 validation events collapse to 7 geometries because a mirror is not an independent sample, and F1 validation is 3 groups / 6 events

the label is constant within an event and on the frozen teacher table it is perfectly confounded with the mirror group (all base events need screen-right, all mirror events need screen-left), so a head could in principle read "which group is this" instead of "where is the gap"; the per-cell table, the offset column and the confusion are reported so that this cannot be hidden
the label is a displacement, not a parking instruction: it never says "hold", and the teacher itself holds at the anchoring row on 6 of 12 labelled events
the auxiliary task is supervised only on the six F1 train events and only inside the telegraph window, so 8 of the 14 update positions carry an exactly-zero auxiliary term
the auxiliary weight (0.5) is fixed before the run and never tuned
the F1 win condition is exact parking inside a 12-20 px gap; it is not tactical understanding
synthetic fixed-y worlds, two-frame actions, no shot, no bomb, no real TH08 pixels
a privileged training-time label is not a route to a deployable policy; research heads only: no formal gate, no deployable checkpoint, no game
